netSalary.h1: Net salary calculator {{year}}: gross to net
netSalary.answer: Net salary is what is left after pension, keren hishtalmut, national insurance and health tax, and income tax. For example, a gross of {{gross}} with {{points}} credit points, {{pension}}% pension and a standard keren hishtalmut comes to about {{net}} net a month. Enter your details below for an instant estimate.
how: Start from the monthly gross salary. Take off your pension and keren hishtalmut deposits (if any), then national insurance and health tax.

Income tax is worked out in brackets on all taxable pay. Credit points are then taken off the tax, each worth {{pointValue}} a month. Your pension deposit also earns a {{pensionCreditPct}}% credit up to a cap, and so do donations.
Employer deposits for pension, severance and keren hishtalmut don't come out of your pay, so they don't change your net. They are part of the employer cost shown.
Credit points depend on sex, children, military or national service, an academic degree, immigration and reserve duty. You can enter them under "Advanced" in the salary card.

faq.q: What is the difference between gross and net salary?
faq.a: Gross is the pay agreed with your employer before deductions. Net is what reaches your account after pension, keren hishtalmut, national insurance and health tax, and income tax.

faq.q: How many credit points am I entitled to?
faq.a: In this calculator a man starts with {{male}} points and a woman with {{female}}. More points are added for children, military or national service, an academic degree, immigration and reserve duty. Your exact amount is set by form 101 and your payslip.

faq.q: Do employer deposits reduce my net pay?
faq.a: No. Employer deposits for pension, severance and keren hishtalmut are paid on top of gross pay. They only appear here as part of the employer cost.

faq.q: Will the result match my payslip?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It is an estimate for a resident employee with one job. Your payslip can also reflect benefits, tax coordination, variable pay and yearly settlement.

seo.description: A compound interest calculator with monthly deposits, yearly return and management fee. Chart and yearly table, runs in your browser, no sign-up.

compoundInterest.answer: With compound interest, each period's gain joins the principal and earns gains of its own. For example, {{initial}} to start plus {{monthly}} a month, at {{returnPct}}% a year and a {{feePct}}% fee, grows in {{years}} years to about {{final}}: {{deposited}} deposited and {{interest}} gained.
compoundInterest.calculatorHeading: Calculate what your savings could grow to
how: Each month the balance grows by the net yearly return (return minus fee) divided by 12, and then the monthly deposit is added.
New balance = previous balance × (1 + (yearly return − fee) ÷ 12) + monthly deposit.
The longer the period, the larger the share of gains in the final amount. Even a small difference in fees matters a lot over decades.

assumptions.depositValue: At the end of each month, after compounding

faq.a: Interest calculated on the gains already earned, not only on the original amount. Growth speeds up as time passes.

faq.q: Is the return I enter guaranteed?
faq.a: No. The calculation assumes a constant return for illustration. Real returns vary from year to year and can be negative.

faq.q: How do fees affect the result?
faq.a: Fees lower the net return every year and the gap compounds. Try 0.5% against 1.5% on the same deposits.
No. It is before capital gains tax and inflation, so it is higher than what you would actually keep.
